subject: FinCorp model evals: next steps & dataset format
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@fincorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: FinCorp model evals on Redwood

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to hear more about the customer service use cases and the 1) entity extraction from support tickets and 2) free-text summarization for agent handoffs. Per our conversation, I put together the recommended next steps and a pragmatic eval plan so we can measure model fit on Redwood and push a small pilot quickly.

Quick summary / recommendations:
- Recommended models to test (initial pass): redwood-qa-xxl (best for closed-book Q&A), open-llm-3b-quant (cost-sensitive baseline), and redwood-instruct-7b (instruction-following).
- Benchmarks & reference: attached a short guide with benchmark links and our internal eval deck (see fincorp-eval-guidelines.pdf).
- Prompt sets: we recommend 3 prompt families — entity extraction (structured labels), summary prompts (concise agent handoff), and reranking prompts (for response selection).
- Quality/regression concerns: for entity extraction we’ll run exact-match + field-level precision/recall; for summaries we’ll run ROUGE/L and a small human review sample to catch hallucination/regression.

Running customer-specific evals on Redwood (what we need from you):
1) Dataset: either CSV or JSONL. Minimum required columns/fields: id, input, expected_response (or labels for extraction), category, and priority. Preference: JSONL with one example per line (see attached spec).
2) Size: start with a 100–500 sample for the first run (helps iterate quickly).
3) Anonymization: remove any PII before upload; if you need, we can help with a scrubber script.
4) Scoring criteria: exact-match for structured entities; ROUGE/BLEU for free text; custom scoring hooks available for business rules (we can map to your ticket taxonomy).
5) Logistics: upload dataset to the Drive folder or a secure S3 bucket we’ll provide; we’ll spin up a temporary eval project and share a read-only results dashboard.

Proposed timeline:
- You share sample dataset by Tue, 2027-04-06
- Kickoff & ingestion call: Wed, 2027-04-07 (30 min)
- Initial eval run & results: within 48–72 hours after ingestion

Next steps for you: send a sample (CSV or JSONL) and confirm whether Drive or S3 works best. I attached our short guidelines and benchmark links to help format the data.

Thanks — looping in Neha and Dev to pick up the technical onboarding and run the harness once we have the sample.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: fincorp-eval-guidelines.pdf

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary — this is exactly what we needed. I attached a 100-row sample (fincorp-sample-100.csv) to get started. A couple quick questions before we upload the full set: 

- Scoring weights: for entity extraction we care about exact-match for high-value fields (account_id, issue_type) — is it possible to set field-weighted scoring so those count more in the overall score?
- Latency / cost metrics: can Redwood also surface token-level latency and a per-model cost estimate for the eval runs? Miguel and I want to understand production economics if we move forward.
- Drive vs S3: we prefer Drive for now (security team will approve S3 later).

We’ll anonymize account numbers in the sample but keep the label columns intact. Please confirm the format you prefer (CSV vs JSONL) and we’ll upload the larger file by the 6th if everything looks good.

Best,
Sofia Alvarez
Head of Product Analytics | FinCorp
sofia.alvarez@fincorp.com

Subject: Re: Next steps: FinCorp model evals on Redwood

Hi Sofia — thanks for the sample, and great questions. Quick answers and the technical ingestion spec below.

1) Scoring weights: yes — our eval harness supports per-field weighting. We can configure the overall score to prioritize account_id and issue_type (you can specify weights in the scoring config). We’ll share a suggested weight proposal (e.g., account_id: 0.4, issue_type: 0.35, other fields: 0.25) and you can adjust.

2) Latency/cost metrics: yes — for each eval run we provide token-level latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), per-token cost estimates based on model pricing tier, and an aggregated per-example cost estimate. We’ll include the cost estimates in the results dashboard so you can compare model economics side-by-side.

3) Preferred dataset format: JSONL is preferred for automated ingestion. Each line should be a JSON object with these fields -> id, input, expected, metadata (optional). For extraction tasks we recommend expected be a dict of labeled fields; for summaries expected should be a text string. If you prefer CSV we can accept it but will convert to JSONL during ingestion — please include a column header row that maps to id,input,expected,category,priority.

4) Anonymization: please scrub PII. For account ids you can use hashed values or reversible tokens. If you need a quick script, we can run a scrub pass before ingestion.

5) Eval harness & scoring criteria (initial config):
- Entity extraction: exact-match + field-level precision/recall; per-field weights configurable. Target: >95% exact-match on account_id (pilot threshold subject to change).
- Summarization: ROUGE-L, ROUGE-1, and a 200-sample human review for hallucination checks.
- Reranking / relevance: MRR and top-1 accuracy.
- Latency: p95 latency target < 300ms on a small dedicated pool for the fastest model; we’ll report p50/p95/p99.
- Cost: per-token and per-example cost estimates in USD using your expected throughput pattern.

6) Upload & access: since you prefer Drive, please upload the dataset to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-fincorp-evals and set sharing to allow the redwood-evals@redwood.com service account to read. If there are controls that prevent service accounts, let us know and we’ll create a short upload form to capture the dataset securely.

7) Next steps and timeline:
- Once we have the dataset in Drive we’ll ingest and run an initial eval (2–3 business days).
- We’ll share a read-only results dashboard (link will look like https://console.redwood.ai/evals/fincorp-evals-202704) and a short summary deck with recommendations.

I attached the eval harness spec (eval-harness-specs.md) with concrete examples for JSONL rows and a sample scoring config. Dev — I’ll hand the ingestion + initial run to you once Sofia confirms upload.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Staff ML Engineer, Model Ops | Redwood Inference
